name: Hi-Tech Gears Ltd
tagline: NSE: HITECHGEAR | Smallcap auto-component (engine/transmission parts) manufacturer, incorporated 1986
business_overview: Manufactures engine and transmission components (gears, forgings, machined parts) supplied to OEMs in India and abroad.
source_notes: Source sheet grouped it with Alan Scott and Samkrg Pistons as having 'lower relative emphasis or more critical/neutral tone' - this research confirms a genuinely weakening fundamental and technical picture.
fundamentals_table: Reduced sharply from Rs 147 Cr (Mar 2024) to Rs 49 Cr (Mar 2026) - a genuine positive
fundamentals_narrative: This is a company in genuine fundamental decline: negative 3-year sales CAGR, negative profit growth at every horizon (worsening to -29% TTM), weak ROCE/ROE, and margin compression (operating margin down to 10.78% in Q1 FY26). The one clear positive is disciplined debt reduction (roughly two-thirds cut in two years). At a P/E of 34.6x, the valuation is not being supported by the growth trend - if anything it looks expensive for a business shrinking on some measures.
technical_read: Weekly: MACD Level -16.17 (Sell), RSI(14) 35.1 (weak, approaching oversold), moving averages overwhelmingly Sell (13 of 14) - a clear, established downtrend. Monthly: MACD Level -9.92 (Sell), RSI(14) 45.3 (neutral-weak), shorter/medium moving averages (10-50) Sell while longer ones (100-200) remain Buy - reflecting that the stock is still above its very long-term base even as its more recent trend has turned down. Read: both timeframes confirm the -17% 1-year price underperformance flagged by Screener - this is a stock in an active downtrend, not one showing early re-rating signs.
sentiment_summary: No high-engagement recent ValuePickr or X discussion was identified in this pass, consistent with the source sheet's characterization of 'lower relative emphasis.'
bse_notes: No red flags found. Promoter holding is high (56.12%) but has a slight declining trend worth monitoring, not a hard red flag on its own.
